nodes.name: Set - Define Reporting Week
nodes.notes: Single place the week boundary and run timestamp are decided (architecture v1 section 5). Added a 6th field, triggeredAt, beyond the architecture's stated 5 fields, so node 20's run_at column has a real timestamp without any node outside this one calling $now. runId duplicates the weekLabel formula rather than referencing the sibling field within the same node, because n8n Set-node assignments cannot reliably read a sibling assignment set moments earlier in the same node call. QA v1 ruling: the $now-count rule is about place, not count -- accepted, no change needed there. MAINTENANCE (QA v1 MINOR 3): 'Europe/London' is hardcoded in FIVE places in this node -- the timezone field itself, plus inside all four $now expressions (weekStart, weekEnd, weekLabel, runId) -- because a Set node cannot make those four expressions read the timezone field beside them. PRD §12 item 9 (time zone) is still OPEN. When it closes, all five must be edited together: search this node's assignments for the literal string 'Europe/London' and change every occurrence, or the node will compute the week boundary against two different time zones at once.

nodes.name: HubSpot - Fetch Deals And Pipeline
nodes.notes: PRD §12 item 4 (which pipeline / which stages count as pipeline) is OPEN and PARKED by Leo. The hs_lastmodifieddate GTE/LT week-bounds filter is a functional placeholder so the node is fully shaped, not the final business filter -- revisit once HubSpot is connected and item 4 is answered. additionalFields.properties is set explicitly to avoid the bare-Deal-ID trap (Integrator report, blocking item 7). authentication is set to 'appToken' (HubSpot Private App / Service Key) because HubSpot has deprecated plain API keys; Leo should create that credential type, not an API Key one. No credential attached -- none exists on this instance yet. RULING v1 (2026-09-14): onError changed from continueRegularOutput to continueErrorOutput so node 9 can ask n8n's router which output this node's items landed on, instead of guessing from item shape.

nodes.name: Supabase - Fetch Product Usage
nodes.notes: PRD §12 item 3 (Supabase project / table / usage fields) is OPEN and PARKED by Leo. tableId, the date column name and orderBy are SET_ME placeholders -- there is no live credential to pick real values from. returnAll is set to true deliberately (Integrator flagged the node's limit default of 50 as a silent-truncation trap). No credential attached. Must be reconfigured once Supabase is connected and item 3 is answered. RULING v1 (2026-09-14): onError changed from continueRegularOutput to continueErrorOutput -- this is the node that started the ruling: a dead Supabase and an empty Google Sheet both emit { json: {} } on the main output, byte for byte, so item shape alone can never tell them apart.

nodes.name: Google Sheets - Fetch Last Week Snapshot
Merge - Wait For All Five Sources
nodes.notes: Five inputs, indexes 0-4, one per fetch node (HubSpot 0, Supabase 1, Finance 2, Support 3, Snapshot 4). Each input is fed by both outputs of its fetch node -- the main output and the error output both land on the same index -- so every input gets at least one item whether that source succeeds or fails (ruling: docs/architecture/v1-source-classification-ruling.md section 4.2). Verified twice on real data, executions 536 and 537: the Merge fired and node 9 emitted exactly one item. What is still unverified: whether chooseBranch/waitForAll waits on inputs or on individual connections. On every run exactly one of the two connections into each input stays silent, and if waitForAll counts connections rather than inputs the Merge could stall here with no error and no alert (QA v3 NEW-5) -- needs a live test before being trusted.

nodes.name: IF - Enough Data To Build Brief?
OpenAI - Write Executive Narrative

values.content: You are writing a short executive narrative for a weekly leadership brief. You will receive one JSON object with computed metrics, pipeline data, revenue trend, a list of missing data sources (missingSources) and a list of empty data sources (emptySources). Rules: (1) Only describe what the numbers in the JSON show. Never invent a cause, a number, or a trend that is not directly computable from the JSON. (2) If missingSources is not empty, say nothing about those areas at all -- do not mention, estimate or infer anything about them, and write as if they do not exist in your narrative. (3) If emptySources is not empty, those areas were read successfully and had nothing in them this week -- you may name them as a real, verified zero, for example "no tickets were logged this week", and you must never describe an empty source as unavailable, missing, or unknown. (4) Cover, in plain business English and under 250 words: major changes, wins, risks, exceptions, and any metric that needs attention (a large variance against target or a large week-over-week change). (5) Do not use markdown headers or bullet formatting -- write plain prose paragraphs suitable for pasting into a document. (6) If dataComplete is false, open with one sentence acknowledging that this week's brief is based on partial data, without naming any number for the missing area.
={{ JSON.stringify($('Code - Normalise And Calculate Metrics').item.json, (k, v) => k === 'sourceDiagnostics' ? undefined : v) }}

nodes.notes: Built DISABLED per money-facts.md -- must stay disabled until QA passes and Leo/Tester explicitly enable it. Model gpt-5-mini chosen live from this credential's real model list on 2026-09-13 (cheapest confirmed-priced model at $0.25 / $2 per 1M tokens per Integrator report). Confirm this is still the right model before enabling. maxTries capped at 2 -- every retry here is a real charge. RULING v1 (2026-09-14): system prompt's rule (3) added -- emptySources may be named as a real verified zero, missingSources stays fully unmentioned. Still disabled, not touched otherwise. QA v3 NEW-8 (2026-09-14): the user-message payload now strips sourceDiagnostics via a JSON.stringify replacer, so the diagnostics block node 9 added for the Tester is never sent to the model. System prompt untouched by this fix.

nodes.notes: Route A from architecture v1 section 8. Riskiest unverified assumption in the whole design (Integrator priority item 3): whether Drive's HTML-to-Doc conversion fetches remote URLs (the QuickChart charts) during conversion. Must be proven with a real throwaway run before being trusted -- if it does not embed images, Route B (three different nodes) replaces this node and node 14. No Drive folder parent is set, so the Doc lands in the credential's My Drive root -- the 'Executive Reporting Rollup' Drive folder referenced in data-sources.md was created under a different, unverified Google account and is not assumed reachable.

nodes.name: IF - Was The Brief Approved?

conditions.leftValue: ={{ ($('Telegram - Request Brief Approval').item.json.data?.approved ?? $('Telegram - Request Brief Approval').item.json.approved) === true }}

nodes.notes: Defensive null-check: the leftValue expression uses a strict === true comparison, so approved being false, null, or completely absent (the unverified timeout case, Integrator report item 6) all evaluate to false and route the same way, to the not-sent branch. Nothing here assumes the approved key exists on the item.

nodes.name: IF - All Sources OK For Snapshot?
Google Sheets - Append Weekly Snapshot Row
nodes.notes: The workflow's only write (PRD §7, CLAUDE.md). Column order matches data-sources.md exactly: week_label, week_start, week_end, run_at, synthetic, notes. synthetic is hardcoded false because this node only ever appends a REAL run's row -- seeded synthetic history is a separate, one-off task, never produced by this node.

nodes.name: Telegram - Alert Brief Not Sent

parameters.text:
={{ (function(){ var approved = ($('Telegram - Request Brief Approval').item.json.data?.approved ?? $('Telegram - Request Brief Approval').item.json.approved); var reason = (approved === false) ? 'The brief was declined.' : 'Nobody responded within the 6-hour approval window.'; var week = $('Code - Normalise And Calculate Metrics').item.json.week.weekLabel; var docId = $('HTTP Request - Create Google Doc From HTML').item.json.id; return 'Brief for ' + week + ' was NOT sent to leadership.
' + reason + '
No snapshot row was written.

Review: https://docs.google.com/document/d/' + docId + '/edit'; })() }}

nodes.notes: Fires on rejection or approval timeout (architecture v1 section 15). Tells the two apart by checking whether approved is exactly false (declined) versus anything else including absent (timed out) -- simpler than, and just as safe as, the timestamp comparison the architecture describes, since the ACTIONS taken (no email, no summary, no row) are identical either way; only the wording differs.

nodes.notes: Error Trigger's exact output shape (workflow.name / execution.lastNodeExecuted / execution.error.message) could not be verified from any node schema -- get_node only describes configurable input parameters, not a trigger's runtime output shape. Written defensively with a try/catch and field fallbacks so this alert itself cannot throw.
